string.text: {=taom_enc_caravan_greet_west_kin}A friendly face on the road is a rare thing these days. We carry grain and good cloth to the markets downriver, and you are welcome at our fire tonight.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_west_friend}Greetings, traveller. Ours is honest trade under the protection of the realm, and if you mean us no harm, we wish you a safe road.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_west_foe}Keep your distance. These goods are bound for our own towns, and our guards are well paid to see that they arrive.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_west_kin}You would rob your own? Take it, then, and may the shame of it ride with you all the way home.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_west_friend}This is a lawful caravan of the realm. Take what you will, but every lord between here and the Sea will learn your name.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_west_foe}Take the goods and be cursed for it. Our captains will hunt you down before the season turns.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_west_kin}Good day to you. It does the heart good to meet one of our own on the market road.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_west_friend}Good day, traveller. We are only taking our harvest to the town, and we have no quarrel with anyone.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_west_foe}Please, let us pass. We have a cart of turnips and a few sacks of barley, and nothing here is worth a soldier's time.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_west_kin}Our grain feeds your own towns. Take it if you must, and the hearths will be colder this winter for it.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_west_friend}We have done you no wrong. Take the cart, then, and may your conscience weigh more than our grain.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_west_foe}Take it and be gone. The lord of these lands will hear of this, and so will the rangers in the hills.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_rohirrim_kin}Well met on the road. We carry wool and leather down to Aldburg, and it is good to see one of our own along the way.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_rohirrim_friend}Greetings, rider. We are bound for Edoras with hides and good saddlery, and we want no trouble on the way.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_rohirrim_foe}Ride wide of us. The road to Edoras is watched by the éoreds of the Mark, and they ride fast.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_rohirrim_kin}Riding down your own neighbours on the road? Take it, then, and carry the shame of it back to your hall.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_rohirrim_friend}We trusted you on this road. Take what you want, but the Riddermark will hear of it.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_rohirrim_foe}Take it, thief. The riders of the Mark will hunt you down before you reach the Fords of Isen.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_rohirrim_kin}Good day to you. We are taking barley and cheese to market at Aldburg, if the weather holds.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_rohirrim_friend}Peace on you, traveller. We are only bringing our harvest to market, and we want no quarrel.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_rohirrim_foe}Stay back from us. One blast of our horn will bring the riders down on you.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_rohirrim_kin}You would take bread from your own neighbours? Then take it, and may no good horse ever carry you again.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_rohirrim_friend}We took you for a friend of the Mark. Take what you came for and be gone.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_rohirrim_foe}Take it, then. The Westfold remembers every raid, and so will the riders who come after you.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_northmen_kin}Ho there, neighbour! Good cloth, dried fish and a cask or two from the south, and a fair price for one of our own.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_northmen_friend}Good day to you. We carry honest wares down the river roads and want no trouble, though we will gladly do some trade.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_northmen_foe}That is near enough. My guards have strung their bows, and there is no trade for you today.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_northmen_kin}Every market from the Lake to the Sea of Rhûn will hear who robbed their own.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_northmen_friend}We dealt fairly with you, and this is how you repay it? Take what you will, then, and be named a thief in every hall of the North.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_northmen_foe}Take it, then, and choke on it. Our kin will come for it before the snows.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_northmen_kin}Well met, neighbour! We are taking the season's honey and wool to market. Walk with us a way, if you like.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_northmen_friend}Good day. We are only taking our harvest to market, and we would be glad of a peaceful road.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_northmen_foe}Leave us be. There is nothing on these carts but grain and wool, and we have families waiting on them.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_northmen_kin}From you, of all people? Our children will go hungry this winter, and it will be your doing.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_northmen_friend}We showed you nothing but kindness. Take it and go, and may your own fields fail.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_northmen_foe}Take it, then. We have rebuilt after worse than you, and we will do it again.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_dunlendings_kin}Good to see a hill face on this road. We carry wool and hides down to the valley markets, so take what you need for the journey.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_dunlendings_friend}Wool, furs and good hill iron, stranger. Fair coin buys fair goods, and we do not haggle long.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_dunlendings_foe}Keep your distance and your hands where we can see them. We carry little worth taking and have less patience.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_dunlendings_kin}You would rob your own? The clan chiefs will hear of this, and they will not speak your name kindly again.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_dunlendings_friend}So your fair words were a lie. Take it, then, and know that Dunland keeps count of every theft.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_dunlendings_foe}One more thief on our roads. Take what you will, and the clans will take it back in blood.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_dunlendings_kin}Welcome, friend of the hills. We are bringing barley and cheese to market, and you may share our bread tonight.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_dunlendings_friend}We are bound for market with what the hills gave us this year, which is little enough. Pass in peace.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_dunlendings_foe}We have nothing for you but sheep and hard words. Let us go on to market.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_dunlendings_kin}Shame on you, robbing your own hearth-kin. The elders of the clan will hear of it, and so will the whole glen.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_dunlendings_friend}Take it, then. Another hungry winter, and one more name to curse by the fireside.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_dunlendings_foe}Thieves on our roads again. Take it and go; the hills will know your face next time.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_southrons_kin}Peace, friend from home. Our beasts carry spice and silk, and the road is easier in good company.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_southrons_friend}Greetings, traveller. We trade fairly and travel peacefully, and we hope you will let us do both.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_southrons_foe}Come no nearer. Our guards are well paid and they know their spears.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_southrons_kin}The whole South will hear of this, and no well will give you water.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_southrons_friend}So this is what your friendship is worth. Take it, then, but every merchant from the havens of Umbar to the far jungles will know your face.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_southrons_foe}Take the goods and choke on them. The serpent banner will have its due for every coin you steal.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_southrons_kin}Peace to you. We take dates and grain to market, and it gladdens us to meet one of our own on the road.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_southrons_friend}Good day, traveller. We are only farmers on the way to market, with nothing worth a quarrel.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_southrons_foe}Please, we are only taking our harvest to market. We have no part in the wars of the great houses.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_southrons_kin}The elders will hear of this, and the sun will see it too.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_southrons_friend}We greeted you kindly, and this is how you repay us. May the sun burn your road dry.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_southrons_foe}Take it, then, and may the heat strike you down before you reach home.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_easterlings_kin}Well met on the road! Come, look over the wagons, and drink the first cup of brew as a guest of my clan.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_easterlings_friend}Greetings, traveller. We carry bronze, hides and steppe horses, and we trade fairly with those who keep the peace.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_easterlings_foe}Keep your hands from your weapons. My guards are riders of the East, and they have killed for less.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_easterlings_kin}From the Sea of Rhûn to the far steppe, the clans will hear how you treat your own wagons.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_easterlings_friend}So your peace was a lie. Take what you want, but the one we serve will come asking for every coin of it.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_easterlings_foe}The wagons will not be given up while one guard still stands. Come and take them if you can.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_easterlings_kin}A face from home! We are bound for market with grain and wool. Ride with us a while if you wish.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_easterlings_friend}Good day to you. We are only farmers of the eastern fields, taking our harvest to sell.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_easterlings_foe}We have no quarrel with you, and nothing worth the taking. Let us pass to the market.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_easterlings_kin}Thieving from your own blood? The elders will spit on your name at every fire in the East.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_easterlings_friend}We took you for a friend. Our chieftain protects these fields, and you will pay for this.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_easterlings_foe}We may be farmers, but our people were warriors first. You will bleed for every sack.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_elves_kin}A familiar face on a weary road. We carry wine, fine cloth and the work of our smiths, at the price we keep for our own.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_elves_friend}Greetings, traveller. Our wares are few but made with care: cloth, wine and blades of old craft, should any please you.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_elves_foe}We know whose banner you follow. Keep your hands from your weapons, and we will pass you by in silence.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_elves_kin}This from one of our own? Take it, then, and carry the shame of it for longer than you can imagine.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_elves_friend}We had thought better of you. Our goods you may seize, but the trust you break today will not be given again.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_elves_foe}Take what you will. Our wardens will learn of this, and they are swift and patient both.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_elves_kin}Be welcome among us. We carry honey, herbs and the gleanings of the woods to market; walk with us a while if you wish.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_elves_friend}Peace to you, traveller. We are bound for market with what the woods have given us this season.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_elves_foe}We are no soldiers, only keepers of the woods and gardens. Let us pass quietly, and we will trouble you not at all.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_elves_kin}You would rob your own kin of the little the woods have given? Then take it, and may the trees remember your face.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_elves_friend}We offered you peace and you answer with this. Take the baskets, and go from our sight.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_elves_foe}Robbing gatherers of herbs and honey is a poor sort of victory. Take them; the woods will grow more long after you are dust.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_dwarves_kin}Hail, cousin! Iron from the deep mines and good work from the forges, bound for honest markets. Ride with us a while if you like.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_dwarves_friend}Good day, traveller. These wagons carry worked steel and silver from the mountains, fair goods for fair coin.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_dwarves_foe}Stay back. We know whose banner you ride under, and every guard here is spoiling for a reason.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_dwarves_kin}You would rob your own kin? The clans will hear of it, and no forge in the mountains will serve you again.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_dwarves_friend}So this is how you repay honest trade. Take it, then, and know the debt will be collected with interest.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_dwarves_foe}Take the goods if you can carry them. Every ingot you steal will be paid back in blood before the year is out.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_dwarves_kin}Well met, cousin. We are taking ore and smithwork down to market, and the road is lighter for a familiar face.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_dwarves_friend}Good day to you. Coal, ore and a few sound blades for the market, if you are buying.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_dwarves_foe}We are only miners carrying ore to market. Leave us be and go about your business.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_dwarves_kin}Our elders will speak your name in the halls, and they will not speak it kindly.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_dwarves_friend}We trusted you on this road. Take what you want, but every one of us will remember your face.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_dwarves_foe}Take it and be cursed. The mountain keeps a long account of thieves, and yours is opened today.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_orcs_kin}Keep your claws off the cargo, every sack is tribute and every sack is counted. Walk with us a while if you like, the road's safer in a crowd.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_orcs_friend}Hold there. These wagons haul tribute for the masters, so say your business and keep moving.
{=taom_enc_caravan_greet_orcs_foe}Get back, you, or the drivers turn their whips on you instead of the slaves.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_orcs_kin}Robbing your own lot? The overseers will hear of this, and they'll skin us both for it.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_orcs_friend}Take it, then, thief. When the masters count the tribute short, they'll come hunting for whoever thinned it.
{=taom_enc_caravan_defy_orcs_foe}Grab it and choke on it. Every crate bears the mark, and the masters never forget a theft.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_orcs_kin}You know the whip as well as we do. Let us by, we're late with the grain and the overseers count the hours.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_orcs_friend}Please, let us pass. If this grain reaches the overseers late, it's our backs that pay.
{=taom_enc_villager_greet_orcs_foe}Don't hurt us! We only work the fields, and the masters own every sack and every one of us.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_orcs_kin}You know what happens when the tribute comes up short. May the whip find you before it finds us.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_orcs_friend}Take it. We get the lash either way, and one more beating hardly matters now.
{=taom_enc_villager_defy_orcs_foe}Take it and be cursed. The masters will flay us for this, and then they'll come looking for you.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_dunland_raiders_kin_1}Easy now, traveller. You have the look of someone who has known a hungry winter, so you know why we ask for your silver.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_dunland_raiders_kin_1}There is sense in you. Half of what you carry will do, and you keep the rest for your own hearth.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_dunland_raiders_kin_1}That will feed the clan until the thaw. Walk safe, and if the horse-lords ask, you saw nobody in these hills.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_dunland_raiders_kin_1}So be it. We bleed the same as you, and we will soon see who bleeds first.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_dunland_raiders_kin_2}We take no joy in robbing our own sort, but the clan comes first. Lay your purse on that stone and walk on.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_dunland_raiders_kin_2}That is the sensible road. A fair share for the clan's pot, and nobody need draw a blade.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_dunland_raiders_kin_2}Kindly done. There is a fire up by the old cairn if the cold catches you on the road.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_dunland_raiders_kin_2}Stubborn as a hill goat, then. Draw, and let the heather judge it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_dunland_raiders_side_1}We may fight the same war, but the war does not feed my clan. Your coin, or we settle it here.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_dunland_raiders_side_1}Good, we keep the peace between us. Give what is fair and our war-chiefs need never hear of it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_dunland_raiders_side_1}Done. Go back to your camp, and keep your band clear of our sheepfolds.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_dunland_raiders_side_1}Then the Shadow will have one servant fewer by nightfall. Take them!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_dunland_raiders_side_2}We march against the same enemies when the war-horns sound, but this pass belongs to the clan. Pay the toll like any other.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_dunland_raiders_side_2}Wise. A share for the toll, and we go back to hating the same enemies.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_dunland_raiders_side_2}Paid in full. When our banners next march the same way, remember the hill clans dealt fairly with you.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_dunland_raiders_side_2}Banner or no banner, nobody shames the clan on its own ground. At them!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_dunland_raiders_foe_1}You ride through hills that were stolen from us once already. Every coin you carry is owed to Dunland twice over.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_dunland_raiders_foe_1}So you can bargain. Empty that purse, all of it, and count yourself lucky we leave you your boots.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_dunland_raiders_foe_1}Go, and tell whoever you serve that the hill clans still remember.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_dunland_raiders_foe_1}Good. I would rather take your silver off a corpse. Bring them down!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_dunland_raiders_foe_2}A long way from home, stranger, and far from any help. The clans have waited years to make one of you pay.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_dunland_raiders_foe_2}Then it will cost you dearly. Every coin in that purse, and be glad we ask no more.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_dunland_raiders_foe_2}One purse does not pay off an old grievance. Get out of the hills before we change our minds.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_dunland_raiders_foe_2}We hoped you would say that. For Dunland and the old wrongs!
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_dunland_raiders_kin_1}Hold your blade! We are only hungry hill clans, and we have done you no wrong. Leave us be and go your way.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_dunland_raiders_kin_2}Why turn on us? We share the same cold and the same short years, and there is nothing here worth the killing.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_dunland_raiders_side_1}You strike at those who fight your own war? The war-chiefs will hear of this treachery.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_dunland_raiders_side_2}Back off! We answer the same war-horns as you. Turn your blades on the horse-lords instead.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_dunland_raiders_foe_1}So someone sends their dogs into our hills now. Come on, then, and learn how the clans fight.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_dunland_raiders_foe_2}Spare us your fine words. We know why you came, and the heather will hide your bones as well as any.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_dunland_raiders_kin}Enough of my clan has died today. Face me alone, blade to blade, and let the winner take what is left.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_dunland_raiders_side}We fight the same war, yet here you stand in my hold with my clan's blood on your blade. Fight me alone and settle it.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_dunland_raiders_foe}You have come deep into Dunland to die. Step forward and face the chief of this clan alone, if you have the stomach.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_rhun_raiders_kin_1}Rein in, traveller. The grass is wide, but every trail across it has a keeper, and the keeper of this one wants your silver.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_rhun_raiders_kin_1}You see sense. A third of your purse, and we will not trouble your wagons.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_rhun_raiders_kin_1}It is enough. Ride on, and drink to us if you ever reach the vineyards of Dorwinion.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_rhun_raiders_kin_1}Then we ride. Make your peace with the sky.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_rhun_raiders_kin_2}The herds were thin this year and the camp must eat. Hand down your silver and we part without a quarrel.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_rhun_raiders_kin_2}A good answer. Give what a herder gives a neighbour in a bad season, and we call it even.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_rhun_raiders_kin_2}The camp will eat tonight because of you. Go in peace while the wind is at your back.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_rhun_raiders_kin_2}A pity. Strike the drums, and let the steppe decide.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_rhun_raiders_side_1}We fight the same war in the end, but the Warlord takes a share of everything that crosses these plains. Pay it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_rhun_raiders_side_1}Good. A fair tithe, and the Eye need not hear that two of its servants quarrelled.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_rhun_raiders_side_1}Paid. Take your band on, and keep it clear of our herds.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_rhun_raiders_side_1}Then the Dark Lord will have a few servants fewer by dusk. Loose!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_rhun_raiders_side_2}Our wagons roll west under the same Shadow as yours, yet these plains keep their own law. Silver for the crossing.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_rhun_raiders_side_2}Spoken like a sensible ally. Name a sum worth my time and we will not haggle long.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_rhun_raiders_side_2}Our quarrel is settled. Save your anger for the Free Peoples and their walls.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_rhun_raiders_side_2}Allies who will not pay are no allies of mine. Ride them down!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_rhun_raiders_foe_1}A stranger on the Warlord's steppe, and alone. Your silver first, and then we will see what else you are worth.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_rhun_raiders_foe_1}You bargain like a captive already. Everything in your purse, and the finest thing in your pack besides.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_rhun_raiders_foe_1}Crawl back the way you came and tell them the East is stirring.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_rhun_raiders_foe_1}Good. The Warlord pays well for enemy heads. Surround them!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_rhun_raiders_foe_2}You wandered too far from your friends. Leave your silver here, and perhaps the vultures go hungry today.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_rhun_raiders_foe_2}Then pay as an enemy pays: every coin, and quickly.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_rhun_raiders_foe_2}Take your empty purse and go. When next we meet, there will be no bargaining.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_rhun_raiders_foe_2}Then the drums speak for us. For Rhûn and the Warlord!
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_rhun_raiders_kin_1}Hold! We are horse herders with lean ponies and empty bellies, like any who live by the road. Let us pass.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_rhun_raiders_kin_2}Why draw on us? The same sun burns us and the same winters starve us. There is no glory in this.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_rhun_raiders_side_1}Lower your weapons! We ride under the same Shadow, and the Warlord will hear who broke faith.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_rhun_raiders_side_2}You would spill the blood of the Dark Lord's own riders? Turn back before this becomes a feud.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_rhun_raiders_foe_1}So you come hunting on our grass. Good, my bow has been idle too long.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_rhun_raiders_foe_2}A long ride for a short life, stranger. Every rider here has sworn to bring your head to the Warlord.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_rhun_raiders_kin}You have fought well enough to earn my respect. Meet me alone, as the old riders did, and the winner keeps the camp.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_rhun_raiders_side}We stand on the same side of this war, and still you burn my camp. Face me alone, and let the steppe judge which of us is stronger.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_rhun_raiders_foe}Your road ends at my fire, stranger. Leave your riders and face me alone, as the steppe has always settled such things.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_harad_raiders_kin_1}Peace, child of the long road. You thirst under the same sun as we do, so you know how this goes. A share of your silver, and we part as friends.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_harad_raiders_kin_1}Good. Between travellers of the same hard road there is no need for spears. Offer what is fair and we will not haggle long.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_harad_raiders_kin_1}It is done, and no blood spilled under the sun. Drink at the oasis to the east and tell them the raiders sent you.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_harad_raiders_kin_1}Then you have chosen badly. Spears level, and let it be quick.

{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_harad_raiders_kin_2}Rest your beasts a moment, traveller. We have little but our spears and a long thirst, and you look like someone who knows what that is. Leave a share of your coin with us.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_harad_raiders_kin_2}I thought you would understand. Count it out in the shade, and we will call it a fair share.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_harad_raiders_kin_2}May your wells run sweet and your road stay free of serpents. We take no more than we need from our own.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_harad_raiders_kin_2}I offered you the courtesy of the road and you spat on it. Then we settle this as the desert settles everything.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_harad_raiders_side_1}The same Eye watches over us both, so we will be gentle about it. Coin for the road, and nobody needs to tell the Tower anything.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_harad_raiders_side_1}Good. Those who fight the same war should not quarrel over trifles. Name a sum and we will call it tribute.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_harad_raiders_side_1}Go on, then. If the captains of the Black Land ask, we never crossed paths.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_harad_raiders_side_1}Then you can explain to the Tower why its servants killed each other in the sand. Spears!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_harad_raiders_side_2}You march in the same war as we do, yet this stretch of desert belongs to the raiders. Every band that crosses it pays, whatever its errand.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_harad_raiders_side_2}So you are no fool. Give us something worth the trouble and we will forget your face before sundown.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_harad_raiders_side_2}Pass, and do not linger near our camps. The sand forgets quickly, and so shall we.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_harad_raiders_side_2}Allies in the war, and still you bare steel at us over a little silver? So be it. Bring them down.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_harad_raiders_foe_1}You are far from any friendly banner, and the desert is wide. Empty your packs into the sand and you may live to curse us.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_harad_raiders_foe_1}So the proud can bend after all. Give generously, for your life is priced high in Harad.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_harad_raiders_foe_1}Crawl back the way you came. The next time the crimson banners find you, there will be no bargaining.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_harad_raiders_foe_1}So be it. Ride them down!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_harad_raiders_foe_2}Look what the wind blew across our sands. A stranger with full packs and no friends within a hundred leagues. Your gold, all of it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_harad_raiders_foe_2}Fear makes everyone sensible. Pour it out where I can see it, and do not hide a single coin.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_harad_raiders_foe_2}Go, and tell whoever you serve that Harad guards its roads with spears. The next toll will be your head.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_harad_raiders_foe_2}Then the sun will bleach your bones before the next moon. At them!
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_harad_raiders_kin_1}Hold your hand! We are only hungry travellers of the sands, the same as you, and nothing in our packs is worth your blood.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_harad_raiders_kin_2}Think before you charge. We have both bled under the same sun, and there is easier prey than us on this road.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_harad_raiders_side_1}Have you lost your wits? We fight for the same Eye. Turn your blades on its enemies and leave us be.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_harad_raiders_side_2}Come on, then, if you think the Tower will thank you for it. The raiders of Harad do not die quietly.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_harad_raiders_foe_1}You ride against the spears of Harad? Many have tried, and the sand keeps every one of them.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_harad_raiders_foe_2}Turn back while you still have water. Our riders know every well and hollow in this waste, and you know none of them.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_harad_raiders_kin}You fight well, for one who shares our sun and our thirst. Face me alone, and let the winner keep the camp without more of my riders dying.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_harad_raiders_side}Enough. The Eye gains nothing if we bleed each other dry. Fight me blade to blade, and the camp goes to whoever is left standing.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_harad_raiders_foe}The sand has swallowed better than you. Come out from behind your spears and face me alone.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gundabad_raiders_kin_1}Hold there, ratling. Even kin pay the toll on Gundabad's road, and the chieftain counts every coin.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gundabad_raiders_kin_1}Sensible. A handful of silver for the chieftain's pot and a bit for us, and nobody tells the wargs you passed.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gundabad_raiders_kin_1}Go on, then. Tell your own warband the Mountain's toll was fair this time.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gundabad_raiders_kin_1}Too proud to pay your own? Then the wargs eat well tonight, kin or no kin.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gundabad_raiders_kin_2}You smell like one of ours, but you walk heavy with plunder. Share it out, or we take the lot.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gundabad_raiders_kin_2}Good. Half of what you carry, and we forget we saw you creeping past the watch-holes.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gundabad_raiders_kin_2}Off with you, quick and quiet. Same cold, same hunger, and today you fed us.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gundabad_raiders_kin_2}Greedy little rat. Hold it down and pick its pockets clean!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gundabad_raiders_side_1}We fight for the same Shadow, but this pass belongs to Gundabad. Pay the toll like any other traveller.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gundabad_raiders_side_1}A purse of silver will do. Your masters can spare it, and ours never feed us enough.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gundabad_raiders_side_1}Pass, then. When the war-drums call, we will remember who paid.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gundabad_raiders_side_1}Allies, you say? Allies bleed the same as anyone. Take them!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gundabad_raiders_side_2}Stop where you are. We bow to the same dark power, but up here the Mountain bites first. Gold, or we bite.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gundabad_raiders_side_2}Fair is fair. A pouch of gold and the food in your packs, and we part as servants of the same Shadow.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gundabad_raiders_side_2}Take the low path out and keep to it. The high caves are ours.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gundabad_raiders_side_2}No toll? Then you can explain it to the chieftain's trolls. At them!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gundabad_raiders_foe_1}Look what crawled up from the valleys. Every scrap you carry, sniveller, or we leave you for the crows.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gundabad_raiders_foe_1}Begging already? Good. All your gold and the boots off your feet, and maybe we let you limp home.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gundabad_raiders_foe_1}Limp away, then. Tell the valleys Gundabad is coming back for the rest.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gundabad_raiders_foe_1}Hoped you would say that. Slit their throats and drag the bodies to the caves!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gundabad_raiders_foe_2}You stand in Gundabad's shadow, worm. Pay the price of the pass, or pay with your hide.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gundabad_raiders_foe_2}Ha! It squeals for terms. Every coin in that purse, and quick, before the wargs grow bored.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gundabad_raiders_foe_2}Crawl off and count your fingers. We may come back for them.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gundabad_raiders_foe_2}Then we take it from your corpse. Wargs, feed!
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gundabad_raiders_kin_1}Hold your blade! The same caves bred us both, so why feed our blood to the crows?
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gundabad_raiders_kin_2}Easy, easy. We only took a few sheep from the valley. Share the meat, and nobody needs to bleed.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gundabad_raiders_side_1}Wait! We answer to the same dark lords. Strike us and the Mountain will hear of it.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gundabad_raiders_side_2}You turn your blades on Gundabad? Your own masters will hang you for breaking the pact, fool.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gundabad_raiders_foe_1}Come up the slope then, valley-rat. Every rock up here hides another of us.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gundabad_raiders_foe_2}Ha! It thinks it can fight Gundabad. We have eaten tougher warriors than you for supper.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_gundabad_raiders_kin}You fought through my warren like one of the deep-born. Face me alone, and the stronger of us keeps the cave.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_gundabad_raiders_side}Allies who raid my caves? Fine. You and me, blade to blade, and the winner takes the spoils.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_gundabad_raiders_foe}You came all this way into the Mountain's gut. Fight me alone, and I will hang your hide over the door.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_umbar_corsairs_kin_1}Easy there, shipmate. You and I both know the price of bread on a hard road. Share your purse with a few honest corsairs and we all eat tonight.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_umbar_corsairs_kin_1}There, I knew you had sense. Lay it on the barrel head and we will split it fair.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_umbar_corsairs_kin_1}Done, and no hard words between us. If you ever want a berth on a fast ship, ask along the quays of Umbar.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_umbar_corsairs_kin_1}A shame. I would sooner have shared a cup with you than bled you. Cutlasses out!

{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_umbar_corsairs_kin_2}Hold up, traveller. We are a long way from the sea, the rations are short, and you look like someone who knows how that feels. A little silver keeps us all friends.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_umbar_corsairs_kin_2}Spoken like someone who has stood a hard watch. Make it a fair share and we will not search your packs.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_umbar_corsairs_kin_2}That will see us back to the ships. May the tide run your way, wherever your road goes.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_umbar_corsairs_kin_2}Pity. I took you for one of us. Over the side with you, then!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_umbar_corsairs_side_1}We answer to no Tower and no White City, and I hear the same is true of you. Still, the coast road takes a toll from everyone who walks it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_umbar_corsairs_side_1}Good. Those who bow to nobody ought to be able to strike a bargain. Name the sum.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_umbar_corsairs_side_1}A clean deal between free blades. If the Captain ever needs hired hands, you know where the ships put in.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_umbar_corsairs_side_1}Then you are no wiser than the kings who would see us both in chains. Have at them!

{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_umbar_corsairs_side_2}Neither the ships of Gondor nor the whips of Mordor have tamed us, and I doubt they tamed you. That makes us near friends, and friends share their silver.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_umbar_corsairs_side_2}I knew we would see eye to eye. Pay what is fair and we will drink to your health tonight.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_umbar_corsairs_side_2}Smooth sailing on dry land, then. The corsairs remember who dealt square with them.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_umbar_corsairs_side_2}So you would rather fight than pay a friend. Then we fight, and the gulls can judge it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_umbar_corsairs_foe_1}Well now, a fat prize walking the coast road alone. Hand over your purse and your boots, and we may let you keep the rest.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_umbar_corsairs_foe_1}Striking your colours already? Wise. Pile it up here, every coin, and be quick about it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_umbar_corsairs_foe_1}Off with you, and pray our ships never sight your shore.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_umbar_corsairs_foe_1}Then we take the prize by force, as Umbar always has. Cut them down!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_umbar_corsairs_foe_2}You have the look of someone who has never been robbed by real corsairs. Today you learn how it is done. Everything you carry, now.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_umbar_corsairs_foe_2}Ha! Not even a fight. Throw it all on the sand, and do not make me count twice.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_umbar_corsairs_foe_2}A rich haul. Go and tell your friends the corsairs come ashore whenever they please.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_umbar_corsairs_foe_2}Good, a fight! Our blades have been dry since the last landfall.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_umbar_corsairs_kin_1}Steady, steady! We are only sailors ashore with empty bellies. Keep your sword in its sheath and we will keep ours.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_umbar_corsairs_kin_2}Think twice, friend. We have both known hard roads and harder captains, and there is no gold here worth the bleeding.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_umbar_corsairs_side_1}You strike at us? We serve no Tower and no White City, and neither do you. Save your steel for those who would chain us both.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_umbar_corsairs_side_2}Mind your aim! The free blades of this coast have few enough friends without cutting each other down.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_umbar_corsairs_foe_1}Come and try it! Every corsair here learned to fight on a pitching deck, and solid ground makes it easy.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_umbar_corsairs_foe_2}A bold charge against the corsairs of Umbar. The sea has drowned bolder, and we sent most of them there.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_umbar_corsairs_kin}Enough of my crew lies bleeding. Face me alone, the way corsairs settle a quarrel, and the winner takes the hold and all in it.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_umbar_corsairs_side}We both keep clear of the great war, so let us settle this freely. One against one, and the cove goes to whoever walks away.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_umbar_corsairs_foe}So you found our cove. Draw and face me alone, and we will see which of us feeds the crabs.

{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gondor_soldiers_kin_1}Easy now, and keep your hand from your sword. You have the look of someone who has stood a long watch too, so pay what you can spare and we part without blood.

{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gondor_soldiers_kin_1}I thought you might see sense. We held the fords while better-fed captains slept, and have nothing to show for it. Name a sum that shames neither of us.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gondor_soldiers_kin_1}That buys bread and a dry barn for a week. Go safely, and if anyone asks, the road was empty.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gondor_soldiers_kin_1}Then draw, and may whoever falls be forgiven. I had hoped someone who knows a hard life would spare us this.

{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gondor_soldiers_kin_2}Hold there. Ten years we stood against the Shadow on the river, and the Steward's clerks forgot our names. Share a little coin with old soldiers, and we all see tomorrow.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gondor_soldiers_kin_2}Good. You know what an empty belly does to tired soldiers. Offer something fair and we will not haggle long.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gondor_soldiers_kin_2}Our thanks. When you sit to your next meal, face west a moment for the comrades we left on the river.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gondor_soldiers_kin_2}So it comes to blades between the likes of us. Shields together, and finish it quickly.

{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gondor_soldiers_side_1}Stop there, friend of the West. We have no quarrel with any who stand against the Shadow, only with empty purses. Lighten yours a little and go on your way.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gondor_soldiers_side_1}Kindly done. We fought for the same cause as you once, before it stopped feeding us. What will you give?
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gondor_soldiers_side_1}The thanks of Gondor, such as it is from the likes of us. Go on, and may your road stay clear of orcs.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gondor_soldiers_side_1}You would rather fight old allies over a few coins? Then guard yourself, and do not expect us to be gentle.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gondor_soldiers_side_2}A moment, traveller. We once held the line so that travellers like you could sleep at night. Call it back pay owed, and hand over some silver.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gondor_soldiers_side_2}Fair of you. The Steward's treasury never was. Name your sum and we will hear it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gondor_soldiers_side_2}That is more than the Tower ever sent us. Go in peace, and may your own lords pay their soldiers better than ours did.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gondor_soldiers_side_2}Then we take it. We are long past caring which side anyone stands on. Steel out!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gondor_soldiers_foe_1}You there, halt! We may have thrown off the Steward's colours, but we still know an enemy when we see one. Your purse, and quickly.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gondor_soldiers_foe_1}You would buy your way past us? Fine, an enemy's coin spends like any other. Make it a heavy offer.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gondor_soldiers_foe_1}Take your road and do not look back. If we meet again, we may not be so hungry.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gondor_soldiers_foe_1}Good. I have missed fighting an honest enemy. At them!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_gondor_soldiers_foe_2}Halt. Our banners are gone, but our swords still remember the enemy. Empty your saddlebags, or we empty them for you.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_gondor_soldiers_foe_2}So you will pay rather than bleed. Clever. Let us see how much your hide is worth to you.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_gondor_soldiers_foe_2}Done. Ride on before some of us decide the coin was not enough.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_gondor_soldiers_foe_2}Then we finish this as we did in the old days in Ithilien. No quarter for those who cross us!
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gondor_soldiers_kin_1}Wait! We have bled for the same lands you ride through. Must it end with us killing each other?
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gondor_soldiers_kin_2}Put up your swords. We are tired, hungry and few, and none of us wants to die on a muddy road for nothing.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gondor_soldiers_side_1}Steady! We once fought beside allies such as you against the Dark Lord. Is this how the Free Peoples repay us?
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gondor_soldiers_side_2}Turn back. We still know how to hold a shield wall, and you will break on it before you break us.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gondor_soldiers_foe_1}So the enemy comes looking for us now. We held against worse on the river, and we will hold here.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_gondor_soldiers_foe_2}Come on, then. Gondor taught us to fight before it forgot us, and we remember every lesson.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_gondor_soldiers_kin}Enough of this slaughter between soldiers. Face me alone, sword to sword, and let my company live or die by how it ends.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_gondor_soldiers_side}I was a captain once, with a banner and a good name. Meet me alone and let the outcome settle this, as was done in the old wars.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_gondor_soldiers_foe}You have come far into our camp, enemy. I will meet you alone, blade to blade, and show you what a captain of the Tower was worth.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_erebor_warriors_kin_1}Well met, cousin of the deep places. Even kin pay toll on this road, though we take less from you than from the rest. Open your purse.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_erebor_warriors_kin_1}Good. No need for axes between those who know the dark under the mountains. Weigh out a fair share.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_erebor_warriors_kin_1}The debt is settled and no beard is bloodied. Go, and do not speak of the Blacklocks in your own halls.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_erebor_warriors_kin_1}So you would raise an axe against your own blood over a little gold. Then you are no better than the ones who drove us out.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_erebor_warriors_kin_2}Stop, kin. The halls that turned us out have done the same to others, maybe to you. Share your gold with the outcast, and we part friends.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_erebor_warriors_kin_2}Spoken like one who knows what it is to lose a hall. Show us the gold and we will be fair with it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_erebor_warriors_kin_2}May the Maker keep you, since the Maker has forgotten us. Walk on, and stay clear of the eastern passes.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_erebor_warriors_kin_2}Then let the old grudge between our houses grow one line longer. Axes!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_erebor_warriors_side_1}We bend the knee to no king, and you keep out of the Dark Lord's war as we do. That makes us neighbours, and neighbours pay toll.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_erebor_warriors_side_1}A neighbourly answer. Show us the coin, and do not hide the good pieces at the bottom.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_erebor_warriors_side_1}Counted and found honest. Go, and if anyone's soldiers come asking, you met no one in these hills.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_erebor_warriors_side_1}We kept out of everyone's wars to keep our gold. Do not think we will lose it to you now. Shields locked, axes high!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_erebor_warriors_side_2}You there. You owe nothing to the great powers, much like us. Still, the road is ours, and the road takes its share in gold.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_erebor_warriors_side_2}Sensible. Those who stay out of the great war have to look after their own purses. What have you got?
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_erebor_warriors_side_2}A clean bargain. Remember that the Blacklocks dealt fairly with you, and deal fairly with us next time.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_erebor_warriors_side_2}Your mistake. We have outlasted kings and worms, and one stubborn traveller will not trouble us long.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_erebor_warriors_foe_1}Hold! You march under a banner, and banners mean wars that were never ours. Pay for passing through our hills, and pay well.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_erebor_warriors_foe_1}So the proud will pay after all. Weigh it out, and we will tell you when it is enough.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_erebor_warriors_foe_1}Taken and written in the book. Go, and tell your lords the hills of the east answer to no one.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_erebor_warriors_foe_1}Good. Our axes have gone too long without work. Break them!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_erebor_warriors_foe_2}Stand fast, stranger. The Blacklocks keep long memories for those who serve the great powers. Your gold, or your blood on the stones.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_erebor_warriors_foe_2}Coin from an enemy is still coin. Set it on the rock where we can see it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_erebor_warriors_foe_2}That pays for this road and nothing more. Cross our hills again and the price will be dearer.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_erebor_warriors_foe_2}Close ranks. We stopped counting enemies the day our halls were taken, and we will not start again with you.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_erebor_warriors_kin_1}Stay your hand! We are of the same stone and the same blood, whatever our banners say.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_erebor_warriors_kin_2}Think on it before you strike. The halls cast us out, but we still swing axes as well as any who stayed.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_erebor_warriors_side_1}Back off. We have no master and no quarrel with you, and you would do well to leave it so.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_erebor_warriors_side_2}Attack the Blacklocks in our own hills? The stones here have drunk better blood than yours.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_erebor_warriors_foe_1}Come then. Every axe in this clan has a grudge to spend, and you will do.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_erebor_warriors_foe_2}Strike, if you dare. The Blacklocks have stood against greater armies than yours and are still here.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_erebor_warriors_kin}You found our hold, kin. Then let it be settled the old way, you and I alone, axe to axe, with the clan as witness.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_erebor_warriors_side}Far enough. I am chief of the Blacklocks, and I will meet you alone before my clan, if you have the stomach for it.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_erebor_warriors_foe}You have broken into the last hall the Blacklocks own. Stand before me alone and earn the right to take it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_mirkwood_stalkers_kin_1}Stand still. You walk with the light step of our own, but exiles cannot live on remembered songs, so your silver comes to us.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_mirkwood_stalkers_kin_1}You remember that the woodland shares what it has. Half of what you carry will do, and we will not count the rest.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_mirkwood_stalkers_kin_1}It is done, and without grief. If the King's wardens ask, you met no one beneath these boughs.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_mirkwood_stalkers_kin_1}So be it. Let the trees see which of us forgot the old songs first.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_mirkwood_stalkers_kin_2}Rest your bow, wanderer. We were cast out of the King's halls long ago and our courtesy went with us, so set down your silver.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_mirkwood_stalkers_kin_2}There is still some sense in the old blood. A fair share and no more, for we have no wish to strip one of our own.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_mirkwood_stalkers_kin_2}Go, and keep to the paths where the light still reaches. Some of us remember how to be kind, though it comes slowly now.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_mirkwood_stalkers_kin_2}Then let the trees bear witness. We will sing for you when it is over.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_mirkwood_stalkers_side_1}Halt there. You owe nothing to any great banner and neither do we, which makes this a plain matter of silver.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_mirkwood_stalkers_side_1}Sensible. Lay a fair portion on that stone, and we will judge whether it is fair.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_mirkwood_stalkers_side_1}Enough. Go your way, and if the Elvenking's wardens find you, you saw only birds in the branches.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_mirkwood_stalkers_side_1}You bargain with blades, then. We have lived too long to fear one more fool in the dark.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_mirkwood_stalkers_side_2}Neither the King nor the Shadow rules this part of the forest. We do, and the toll is paid in silver.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_mirkwood_stalkers_side_2}No great power stands behind either of us, so let us keep this small. A third of your purse will settle it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_mirkwood_stalkers_side_2}That will serve. Follow the stream until the trees thin, and do not leave the water after dusk.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_mirkwood_stalkers_side_2}A poor choice. Your bones will be green with moss before the moon is full.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_mirkwood_stalkers_foe_1}You walk this forest uninvited, under a banner we have no love for. Pay for every step, or lie here until the leaves cover you.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_mirkwood_stalkers_foe_1}Then pay well, for we have little mercy left for the cause you serve. All the gold you carry, and quickly.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_mirkwood_stalkers_foe_1}Go before we think better of it. If your banner passes beneath these trees again, no gold will save it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_mirkwood_stalkers_foe_1}Then the forest will have you. Loose!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_mirkwood_stalkers_foe_2}The spiders took our kin and the King took our homes, so we take what we please from strangers. Coin now, or blood.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_mirkwood_stalkers_foe_2}A coward's bargain, but we will take it. Empty your purse to the last coin and step back from it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_mirkwood_stalkers_foe_2}Begone. The forest forgets nothing, and neither do we.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_mirkwood_stalkers_foe_2}Then learn why travellers fear the dark under the trees. Shoot!
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_mirkwood_stalkers_kin_1}Would you hunt your own beneath the trees? Lower your blade, and we will forget you ever came.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_mirkwood_stalkers_kin_2}We were sent out of the King's halls once already. Must you finish what the King began?
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_mirkwood_stalkers_side_1}We have no quarrel with you and no master to send after you. Ride on and leave us to the dark.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_mirkwood_stalkers_side_2}Careful. We know every root and hollow of this forest, and you know none of them.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_mirkwood_stalkers_foe_1}Come, then. We have fought worse than you in this darkness, and outlived them all.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_mirkwood_stalkers_foe_2}Strike if you dare. This forest has swallowed armies, and it will hardly notice you.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_mirkwood_stalkers_kin}Enough of our blood has stained these roots. Face me alone, one exile against one wanderer, and let the trees judge between us.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_mirkwood_stalkers_side}You found our hollow, which few ever do. Meet me alone beneath the great oak, and whoever falls, the rest go free.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_mirkwood_stalkers_foe}I have kept this hollow since long before you drew breath. Face me alone if you have the nerve, and let the others watch.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_feral_orcs_kin_1}Hungry, hungry. You are one of us, so we ask nice once. Give food and shiny, or we eat yours.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_feral_orcs_kin_1}Good, good. Throw down the meat bag and a fistful of coin. Den shares, den lives.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_feral_orcs_kin_1}Go, go. No whips out here, no masters. Come back when you are hungry too.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_feral_orcs_kin_1}Not sharing? Then the den eats you, bones and all!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_feral_orcs_kin_2}We smell it on you, the whip-scars and the hunger. Out here nobody owns us. Pay the den or bleed for it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_feral_orcs_kin_2}Yes. Half your bread, all your shiny. Then we let you run.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_feral_orcs_kin_2}Gone now. Tell the other runaways the den is fat this season.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_feral_orcs_kin_2}Thinks it is bigger than us! Bite it! Biggest gets first pick!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_feral_orcs_side_1}Stop! Your masters in their towers mean nothing here. In the wild we eat what we catch, and we caught you.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_feral_orcs_side_1}Meat and coin, lots of it. Drop it on the ground and back away slow.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_feral_orcs_side_1}Run back to your masters, then. Tell them the dens bow to nobody.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_feral_orcs_side_1}No pay? Good! Coin is cold and flesh is warm. Get it!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_feral_orcs_side_2}You march for the Shadow? We do not. Out here only the strongest rules, and the strongest says pay.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_feral_orcs_side_2}Leave the pack beasts and the purse. We are not greedy, only hungry.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_feral_orcs_side_2}Walk now, while the den is busy eating. Do not look back.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_feral_orcs_side_2}Then we take beasts, purse and you. Rip!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_feral_orcs_foe_1}Food! Food walking in the wild! Throw down everything, or we pull you down and eat.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_feral_orcs_foe_1}It wants to bargain. All the food, all the shiny, every last crumb, and maybe we only bite a little.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_feral_orcs_foe_1}Run, run far. Next time the den is hungrier.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_feral_orcs_foe_1}Good, it fights! Hot blood tastes better!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_feral_orcs_foe_2}No road here, no lord, no law. Just the den, and the den wants what you carry.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_feral_orcs_foe_2}Clever. Empty the sacks, drop the blades, and crawl past on your belly.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_feral_orcs_foe_2}Crawl on, then. We know your scent now, and we will smell you coming.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_feral_orcs_foe_2}Too slow to pay, too slow to run. Pull it down!
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_feral_orcs_kin_1}No, no! Same blood, same hunger! Why hunt your own when the valleys are full of fat prey?
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_feral_orcs_kin_2}Put it down! We ran from the whips and the pits, same as any of us would. Let the den be.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_feral_orcs_side_1}Hah, the Shadow sends its hounds after us now? We bow to no tower. Come and bleed.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_feral_orcs_side_2}Leave the den alone! We took nothing of your masters'. Only sheep, only stragglers.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_feral_orcs_foe_1}You come to the den? Good. The den was hungry, and now the food comes by itself.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_feral_orcs_foe_2}Wait! Wait! Take bones, shinies, anything! Just do not burn the den!
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_feral_orcs_kin}You smell strong. The den follows the strongest, so fight me alone, and whoever stands keeps the den.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_feral_orcs_side}No master I bow to sent you here. Fight me, just you and me, and the den eats the loser.
{=taom_enc_hideout_boss_feral_orcs_foe}Biggest in the den, me. You want the den, you beat me, one on one, teeth and iron.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_looters_kin_1}Easy now, we were farmers before the war burned the barns. Hand over a little coin and nobody bleeds on this road.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_looters_kin_1}You look like you have known lean winters too. A few coins and a loaf if you have one, that is all we ask.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_looters_kin_1}That will keep the children fed a while. Go on, and may the road treat you better than it treated us.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_looters_kin_1}Then you are no better than the raiders who took everything. Get at them!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_looters_kin_2}Stop there, friend. The war took our fields and our lord forgot us, so the road is the only field we have left to reap.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_looters_kin_2}We are not thieves by trade. Give what you can spare and we will call it fair.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_looters_kin_2}Thank you, truly. Watch the ford ahead, other raiders have been about.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_looters_kin_2}We buried too many this winter to fear one more grave. Come on, then!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_looters_side_1}Hold up! Nobody rides to avenge anyone out here, and we have not eaten in two days, so give us your coin.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_looters_side_1}No need for blades. Some silver and whatever food you carry, and we will let you be.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_looters_side_1}Go on, then. Mind the burned village past the hill, there are worse than us sleeping in its cellars.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_looters_side_1}Hunger makes a body brave. At them!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_looters_side_2}We care nothing for whose banner you follow, or whether you follow any. An empty belly takes no side, so pay up.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_looters_side_2}That is more like it. Half of what jingles in your purse, and keep the rest for your own troubles.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_looters_side_2}Fair enough. The roads have gone bad everywhere since the Shadow rose, so keep your eyes open.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_looters_side_2}Stubborn, are you? We have nothing left to lose but our lives, and those are not worth much.
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_looters_foe_1}Your war burned our homes and left us to starve by the roadside. Now you can pay for some of it.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_looters_foe_1}Pay, then, and pay heavy. Every coin you hand over is one your lords owe us.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_looters_foe_1}Take your road and your war away from here. We have nothing left for either.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_looters_foe_1}Then we take it from your corpse! For the farms they burned!
{=taom_enc_robbery_threat_looters_foe_2}Armies marched through our valley and left only ash, and you ride under their banners. Empty your purse.
{=taom_enc_robbery_pay_agreement_looters_foe_2}Smart. Everything you carry, the food first, then the coin.
{=taom_enc_robbery_conclusion_looters_foe_2}Get out of our sight before we think better of it. Hunger makes poor judges.
{=taom_enc_robbery_start_fight_looters_foe_2}Better to die fighting than starve in a ditch. Have at them!
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_looters_kin_1}Mercy! We are only hungry folk who lost our farms, the same as half the realm.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_looters_kin_2}Wait, we are no raiders! Just poor farmers driven off our land, and we would sooner run than fight you.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_looters_side_1}We have nothing worth taking, only rags and an empty pot. Leave us be and go your way.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_looters_side_2}Come no closer! We starved through one winter already, and we will not die easy in this one.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_looters_foe_1}Back off! Your armies took our harvest, and you will not take our lives as well.
{=taom_enc_bandit_greet_looters_foe_2}Go on, then, cut us down. It is quicker than hunger.
